messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P1high memory/latency anomaly detected for pool 'eu-central-1-paged-1' - automated incident I-2024-238 created.
incident-bot: Key symptoms: sustained 95th latency >1.8s, rapid block_count growth, metadata map expansion, several containers hitting OOM_KILL.
sam (oncall): Observed a correlated jump after the midnight rollout of batching throttle changes. Paging rate has doubled and blockmgr retained_blocks seems not evicting. Immediate customer impact: a handful of teams reporting clipped completions and 5xx errors.
nina (support): Two paying customers reported truncated generations and increased 429/503s. I've escalated and told them we're investigating and applying mitigations.
lee (eng-runtime): Initial probe: block size histogram shows a mode shift to larger blocks (256KB+) which increases per-block metadata. Eviction scanning seems stuck in a slow path. Hypothesis: blockmgr eviction window and batch coalescing combine to produce metadata churn that isn't reclaimed due to a logic bug.
amal (sre): Telemetry snapshot:
```n
kv_block_count=4.1M
metadata_map_size=28M
eviction_candidates_queue=0 (stuck)
continuous_batching_enabled=true
p95_latency=1.92s
```n
This looks like a leak + eviction deadlock.
sam (oncall): Prioritize quick-stop mitigations: A) temporary per-pool rate limit to reduce new allocations, B) shrink configured max_block_size and force block compaction, C) disable the new coalescing path. Propose sequence: rate limit -> shrink -> compaction -> disable coalesce if needed.
lee (eng-runtime): I'll apply the rate limit and perform hot-config to lower max_block_size from 512k -> 64k. Rate-limit command: 
```n
redwoodctl pool update eu-central-1-paged-1 --qps-cap 1200 --reason "incident 1764209999"
```n
Applying now.
[22:13:24] infra-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: QPS cap 1200 applied to eu-central-1-paged-1 by lee (eng-runtime).
amal (sre): After QPS cap: queue depth down 70%, new block allocations reduced by ~60% within 30s, but metadata_map_size still high from existing entries. Need compaction.
lee (eng-runtime): Hotpatch to shrink block size and trigger compaction: 
```n
echo '{"max_block_size":65536, "force_compact": true, "eviction_policy": "aggressive"}' | redwoodctl blockmgr apply-config --pool eu-central-1-paged-1
```n
Rolling it now with 2s stagger per node.
[22:16:10] infra-bot: CONFIG APPLY: blockmgr config applied to eu-central-1-paged-1 by lee (eng-runtime).
nina (support): Customer update sent: "We've applied emergency throttles and maintenance to reduce memory usage. You may notice slightly increased latency while we compact caches. We'll follow up with details."
amal (sre): Compaction job kicked off; CPU spike expected but throttled concurrency to 6 to avoid syscall storms. Observed compaction progress: reclaimed ~14M metadata entries in first 120s. OOM events declining but one pod still in restart loop.
sam (oncall): If compaction doesn't stabilise within 10 minutes, prepare to disable continuous batching and fallback to legacy batching. Which command for that?
lee (eng-runtime): Command to disable coalescing/cohort batching: 
```n
redwoodctl feature toggle --pool eu-central-1-paged-1 --feature batch_coalesce --enabled false
```n
I'll hold off until we see compaction results.
[22:21:52] amal (sre): Metrics now: metadata_map_size 28M -> 9.2M; block_count 4.1M -> 1.3M; p95 latency 1.92s -> 680ms; OOMs reduced to 0 after compaction finishes. Looks effective.
sam (oncall): Good. Move to containment: keep QPS cap for 1 hour, leave block size reduced, and schedule a controlled rollback of the batching change to a canary group. Also create an alert for metadata_map_size > 2M to catch re-accumulation.
infra-bot: ALERT RULE CREATED: metadata_map_size_threshold=2_000_000 for eu-central-1-paged-1; notify oncall and eng-runtime.
lee (eng-runtime): Root cause next steps: gather heapdumps from two worst-hit processes, capture block index snapshot and reconcile with request traces. Planning a backport: ensure eviction scan can't be starved when continuous batches create many small deltas. Will open a PR and include stress-reproducer.
nina (support): Customers acknowledged interim update and requested timeline for fix. I've proposed a technical sync tomorrow and added them to the follow-up thread.
amal (sre): Creating follow-ups: ticket INC-FIX-891 (blockmgr eviction starvation), INC-FIX-892 (batching canary + telemetry), INC-FIX-893 (customer impact audit).
sam (oncall): Lowering incident severity to P3 - system stable under mitigations. Handoff notes: 
- Trigger: batching rollout changed allocation patterns -> larger block sizes + eviction starvation -> metadata growth and OOMs.
- Containment: QPS cap, block size shrink, forced compaction, created alert threshold.
- Impact: transient errors and higher latency for some customers for ~14 minutes.
- Followups: backport eviction fix, add per-request metadata budget, canary future batching rollouts, add compaction health metric.
lee (eng-runtime): I'll produce the postmortem draft and include the heap profiles and step-by-step reproducer. Assigning to myself for the code fix.
amal (sre): Keeping watch on metric alarms for 24h. Reopen incident if metadata_map_size > 2M.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: incident 1764209999 moved to post-incident state. Closing slack thread; please update tickets and append logs.
nina (support): Sending final customer note and scheduling follow-up sync. :white_check_mark:
[Postmortem pointers attached in ticket INC-FIX-891]
